Subject: Post-call recap + next steps: Reranking evaluation for Acme

Thanks again for taking the time earlier, Samir — good conversation and clear requirements. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment: 

Summary of use case (from call):
- Product: Acme Search web/product search; current stack uses BM25 retrieval + lightweight neural reranker for top-50.
- Primary objective: Improve relevance for product queries (commercial intent) and long-tail queries while keeping p99 latency under 120ms for reranking path.
- Signals: Click-through and purchase conversion are primary business signals; have labeled test set (10k queries) and can provide a 1k sample now.

What Redwood will propose/do next:
1) Run an offline reranking fit/eval on your sample set (1k) and, if results look good, repeat for the full 10k dev set.
2) Provide recommended model variants (cross-encoder, distilled cross-encoder, embedding+light re-rank) with NDCG@10 and MRR results, plus cost/latency estimates.
3) Share prompt sets and evaluation harness (negative sampling strategy, metrics, train/val split) so you can review for fairness/regression concerns.
4) Propose an A/B rollout plan (5% canary -> 25% -> 100%) with guardrails and rollback thresholds.

Questions / asks for you (Samir):
- Please share the 1k sample file and an example of the labeled relevance judgments (or confirm the format we saw on the call).
- Any constraints on PII/hosting (we discussed read-only S3 + VPN access if needed).
- Which metric is the single most important for you? (NDCG@10, MRR, CTR uplift, or conversions)

Attachments: acme_reqs_v1.pdf (notes from discovery). Also recording of the call will be added to the Drive link.

Tentative timeline: initial offline eval on the 1k sample within 3 business days after we receive the file; A/B sandbox endpoint for online testing within 7–10 business days if offline results justify.

Next step: Samir to share sample and permission; Rishi will own the eval and share a short results deck.

Thanks,
Marissa
Account Exec, Redwood Inference

Date: Mon, 16 Feb 2026 09:20:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Reranking evaluation plan & preliminary results (1k sample)

Hi Samir / Marissa — I ran the first-pass offline eval on the 1k sample you shared. High-level findings and recommendations below. Full CSV + prompt sets attached (rerank_eval_20260215.csv, prompt_sets_v2.txt) and a short Drive deck here: https://drive.redwood.ai/share/rerank-eval-20260215

Eval setup (quick):
- Retrieval: top-100 BM25 (as you use today), reranker re-scores top-100.
- Neg sampling: in-batch negatives + random negatives drawn from top-100.
- Metrics: NDCG@10 (primary), MRR, CTR proxy (click-weighted NDCG).

Baseline (BM25 only):
- NDCG@10: 0.378
- MRR: 0.312

Model variants tested (in order of preference):
1) redwood-rerank-cross-1 (cross-encoder, 13B fine-tuned on product relevance) — best quality
   - NDCG@10: 0.642
   - MRR: 0.508
   - Median latency (rerank only): 85ms (CPU offload + optimized kernel); p95 140ms
   - Cost: ~2.8x tokens/op relative to your current lightweight model

2) redwood-rerank-lite (distilled cross-encoder, 2.7B) — good quality/latency tradeoff
   - NDCG@10: 0.601
   - MRR: 0.472
   - Median latency: 46ms; p95 95ms
   - Cost: ~1.2x relative to current lightweight model

3) embed_then_light_rerank (sparse+dense hybrid, offline embedding + cheap cross-encoder on top-50)
   - NDCG@10: 0.588
   - MRR: 0.451
   - Good when you want to pre-compute embeddings and reduce online cost

Notes on evaluation quality / concerns:
- Domain shift: performance drops for unseen long-tail queries (as Samir noted). The largest delta vs baseline occurs on product attribute queries.
- Quantization/latency tradeoffs: 8-bit quantization introduces small perturbations — we saw up to -1.8% relative NDCG on a subset. Recommend running quantization-aware evals on the full 10k before committing to a production quantized profile.
- Prompt/format sensitivity: for the cross-encoder we used the prompt templates in prompt_sets_v2.txt. Small prompt changes (stop words, punctuation) shifted ranking of edge cases; we'll provide deterministic prompt A/B variants in the sandbox.

A/B test plan (proposed):
- Phase 0 (offline): full 10k eval, quantization-aware checks, and QA on prompt sets (3 business days once we have the 10k).
- Phase 1 (canary): 5% online traffic for 14 days. Primary metric: weighted NDCG@10 uplift vs baseline; secondary: CTR and conversion lift. Guardrails: if p95 latency > 200ms or cost per query > 3x baseline for 3 consecutive days -> automatic rollback.
- Phase 2: 25% traffic for 7 days if canary passes; then gradual scale to 100%.

Deliverables and timeline (if you share full 10k now):
- Initial full-10k offline eval + quantization-aware pass: 3 business days (deliver rerank_eval_20260215.csv).
- Sandbox endpoint with redwood-rerank-lite and redwood-rerank-cross-1 available for traffic testing: 7 business days.
- A/B monitoring dashboard and automatic rollback policy set up in Console.

Next steps from us: I'll start the full 10k run as soon as we get the presigned S3 link; will also run a quantization sweep for the top candidates and include a short notes section on regression risk.

If helpful, we can also run a small synthetic stress test to estimate p99 under your qps.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Senior ML Engineer, Redwood Inference
